column5: Text is a fragment of a report string; no defect or behaviour can be read from it.
Text gives only a location in a lint rule; no defect stated, and the ticket does not mention lint.
Criterion 5 and C5 give an unrequested surface no verifier folder, so unknown verifier folders must be caught.
Test time limits are a repository rule the ticket's criteria and checks do not reach; one sane fix.
Criteria 2 and 3 have a revised spec approved after changes; a stale changes decision re-triggering is a bug.
Criterion 4 fixes the two-approved bar; branch selection counting from nothing named is the runbook's own gap.
Criterion 4 counts approved workhorse specs; a typo lane is no workhorse, so counting it is plainly wrong.
Verifying the right repository is required under any reading; clearing inherited GIT_* has one sane answer.
Ticket never says what exit status a failed copy removal gets when the fallback left no residue.
A failed install hidden behind a multi-statement gate yields a false pass; any reading requires the failure to surface.
Ticket leaves where the clean copy lives and how far it resists other local accounts to the fix.
Install must follow the project's lockfile as verify.sh already does; one sane answer, one lockfile shape mishandled.
Ticket never says what happens when the gate hangs; the timeout value and containment were chosen by the fix.
Gate runner must follow the same lockfile detection as install; one sane answer, yarn and bun shapes mishandled.
Criterion 2 says a project must never name a credential; bare and camelCase names passing contradicts it.
Criterion 3 requires each lane's own session exported; matching a decoy by suffix is wrong under any reading.
Export must identify the lane's own session; a nested id beating the top-level identity is a wrong match.
Ticket never says what happens when several store records match one thread: newest, refuse or all.
Self-test failing because it inherits the project variable is a plain defect; the ticket requires no particular behaviour.
Criterion 2 forbids naming a credential; camelCase continuations such as secretKey passing contradicts it.
Flow-owned stream path overwritten by an env file sourced first; ordering with one sane answer, outside the ticket.
Left boundary is vacuous under IGNORECASE, so the regex cannot do what its own documentation says.
Export must pick the lane's own thread; a dash-suffix match returning another thread is wrong under any reading.
Ticket never says what an explicitly empty --project does: behave as absent or be refused.
Criterion 2 records a refused launch as refused before any thread; backfilling a stale thread contradicts it.
Lock ownership by inference is a race defect in the launcher; the ticket offers no choice here.
An exit trap releasing a lock it may not own is a plain ownership bug with one sane fix.
Ticket makes walled an outcome but never says which stderr wordings or status numbers count as a wall.
Appending after a torn record without a newline fuses lines; any reading requires a clean line break.
Same torn-tail fuse at a second append site; one sane answer, not a ticket choice.
Claim check-then-replace race lets two legs run live; an atomic claim is required under any reading.
Criterion 4 says a refused resume delivers its prompt once answered; a kill in the gap loses it.
Criterion 1 records each attempt mechanically; an earlier attempt taking a later launch's thread is a bug.
Criteria 3 and 4 need the next action from the record; a stale NEXT burying a refused resume breaks it.
Runbook command names the live tool root instead of the run's pinned checkout; a wrong sentence with one fix.
Criterion 2 records an attempt without its hand-off as such; a stale done marker finishing it contradicts that.
Ticket does not say whether an incomplete outcome or the planning pause wins in next-action precedence.
Hiding a real criterion behind a comment opener in a code span defeats 'every criterion has evidence'; reference counts two.
Ticket makes the not-shown reason free text; a slash in it failing as a path is a wrong classification.
An unclosed comment marker inside a code fence must not hide later entries; one sane reading, a parser shape.
Ticket does not say how a not-shown line trailing or continuing an evidence entry is read.
Section end rule differs from the reference reader; both must list the same criteria, so one sane answer.
Unclosed opener latching comment mode makes script and reference list different criteria; agreement is required.
Criterion 6 needs each cited evidence path checked; skipping a second citation on a line breaks it.
Entry indent rule contradicts the criteria rule in the same script; an indented entry is wrongly reported missing.
A fenced list item body stays readable; script and reference list different criteria, so it must agree.
A bare hash heading ends the section in the reference reader; the script reads one criterion too many.
Ticket does not say where a transcript is cited when every criterion is not shown; runbook and checker disagree.
Criterion 5 says a tripped copy does not complete and a ruling is recorded; partials and gaps break it.
A scan that could not enumerate files passing clean defeats criterion 8; one sane answer is to fault.
Criterion 7 needs the wiki scan to run; silently skipping it outside git is a wrong guard.
Criterion 1 names .env-style assignments of anything key-like; an unquoted value with a comment shape is missed.
Criterion 1 names home-directory paths; a bare home directory before a quote or space is missed.
Criterion 1 scans every commit's added lines; skipping lines that start '++ ' is a diff misparse.
Criterion 1 rules for listed kinds must fire in JSONL transcripts, the incident's own format; they never fire.
A diff hunk shape raising KeyError and exit 2 swallowing findings is a crash under any reading.
Criterion 5 and the recheck must not publish secret fragments; same-line multi-span scrub corrupts the copy.
Criterion 1 says anything that looks like private data; private-shaped file names passing is a missed shape.
Ticket asks only for a reviewable allow record; whether suppressed detections must also be logged is unstated.
Run lifecycle states are outside the ticket; an untold detection still needing telling has one sane answer.
A failed enumeration exiting 0 hides a failure; criterion 3 gives the script its own exit code.
Criterion 3 says never print the value; a copy failure printing a private-shaped path repeats that rule's gap.
Scrub must leave unmatched content intact; re-encoding invalid UTF-8 outside the span corrupts the copy.
Criterion 12 says stream large files; promotion, merge and lint paths buffering break the same rule.
Criterion 5 scans before the copy completes; a change between scan and copy landing dirty content breaks it.
Ticket is silent on whether an allow may suppress the wiki path rule of criterion 7.
Criterion 3 says never print the value; a lint fault printing a private-shaped file name repeats the gap.
Criterion 4 allows one recorded match; a marker silencing other values on its line goes beyond it.
Criterion 1 names private keys in common shapes; a PEM body surviving the scrub contradicts it.
Criterion 8 runs the script on every change; an inherited variable silently blinding it defeats that.
Ticket says common shapes and calls the scan a backstop; how far escape sequences are looked through is unstated.
Criterion 3 lists suspects by file and line without values; reporting a private-shaped path or line 0 is unstated.
Ticket does not say which escape encodings are decoded before matching; raw versus JSON-escaped handling is a choice.
Ticket does not say how deeply nested JSON encodings are decoded; any bound is a choice.
Criterion 4 allows one recorded match; a marker inside record data silencing the next record goes beyond it.
Criterion 1 names .env-style assignments of anything key-like; compound secret names passing contradicts it.
Criterion 1 names private keys in common shapes; PGP, PuTTY, SSH2 and age keys being silent contradicts it.
Criterion 1 scans every commit base to head; empty range after a dirty merge breaks it; challenges round-2 disposition.
Criterion 5 recheck must catch what remains; overlapping spans leaving a tail with a clean report is wrong.
Text lists eight fixes, not a defect; too short to tell what the finding says.
Criterion 3 sends quota or provider walls to the postmaster; wordings with underscore or hyphen separators are missed.
Criterion 3 wakes the postmaster on a launch refusal; a host prefix hiding it contradicts that.
Criterion 1 dispatches each next leg once; a guard testing the wrong marker permits re-dispatch.
Guard against double dispatch misses a launch live but silent; one sane answer, not a ticket choice.
Skip counted newlines, not lines, so an unterminated last line is miscounted; a plain counting bug.
Criterion 3 wakes on a wall; inflected wall wordings falling through is a missed wording, not an open choice.
Criterion 3 wakes on a wall; natural provider phrasings missed is wrong against the stated behaviour.
Criterion 3 wakes on a wall; a three-word span missing real quota text is a missed wording.
Criterion 3 wakes on a wall; a trailing boundary missing snake case suffixes is a missed wording.
Criterion 3 wakes on a wall; structured wall type names not recognised is a missed shape.
Criterion 3 wakes on a wall; a 100-line window missing an early wall resumes wrongly.
Criterion 3 wakes on a wall; stemless 'slow down' wall text being resumed contradicts it.
Ticket never says what the veto scans; ruling chose raw lines anywhere, finding objects, JSON keys then excluded.
Ticket never says how digit stems are bounded; the ruling's no-boundary choice lets ordinary numbers veto.
Ruling already makes unknown structured values wake; one outside the scan window being missed breaks it.
Criterion 3 wakes on a wall; a key allowlist missing wall fields lets a wall be resumed.
Criterion 2 resumes on a named transient; a host notice vetoing every uncapped launch defeats it.
Criteria 2 and 3 need endings classified; error record shapes the adapter attests being missed is a gap.
A corrupt manifest leg misdispatching or killing the watcher is a missing guard with one sane answer.
Criterion 3 wakes on a launch refusal; logging a refused resume as success contradicts it.
Error records nested one level deeper going unmarked is a missed shape; stated behaviour needs them found.
Criterion 3 wakes on a launch refusal; a truncated err file making refusal_since miss it breaks that.
Success statuses 2xx and 3xx blocking a resume contradict criterion 2; only error statuses can matter.
Criterion 2 resumes only on the provider's transient error; a tool subtree's 503 is not one.
Criterion 1 and D5 list TypeScript's ignore comments; a triple-slash ts-ignore reported clear contradicts them.
Criterion 1 and D5 list TypeScript's ignore comments; a triple-slash ts-ignore reported clear contradicts them.
Text is only a location; what is wrong with the quote scan cannot be read.
D8 holds an approval only for the same code; an identity missing an implicit continuation breaks it.
Criterion 7 requires the user's words recorded; a one-token entry passing without words contradicts it.
Criterion 6 says approve each one but D8 identifies by comment and code; identical duplicates are unspecified.
D8 keeps approval for the same comment over the same code; whether enclosing context counts is unstated.
Criterion 11 puts branches back; inheriting GIT_DIR so reset targets another worktree is wrong under any reading.
Criterion 5 lists every write from the lane's record; a write inside a quoted substitution is missed.
Text is a location and half a sentence on change ownership; the defect cannot be read.
Criterion 11 puts branches back as before the round; failing when a reviewer detached the worktree breaks it.
D13 says an unreadable record is reported not checked, never clean; malformed task logs read as empty contradicts it.
Ticket does not say which command operands count as paths; an earlier fix narrowed this and the finding widens it.
D18 shows outside paths only as outside; not-checked reasons printing them verbatim miss the same rule.
Text is only locations and a severity note; the defect in quoted substitution handling cannot be read.
A repository path with a space breaking the profile regex is a plain parsing bug, one sane fix.
Criterion 11 restores the branch to its snapshot; a reviewer-deleted ref making restore fault breaks it.
